where: Section 1, pseudorange formula and its symbol list
problem: The formula and the definition of t_r contradict each other, so the bias is counted twice. The text defines t_r as 'the receive time by the receiver clock'. If t_r is the clock reading, then c(t_r − t_s) already contains the receiver clock bias, and adding c δt_r on top makes the pseudorange too long by a second time. The worked example and the exam trap ('a receiver clock ahead gives pseudoranges that are too long; subtract the error') use the correct physics, so a student who reads the formula literally will be confused about sign and size.
fix: Make the sentence match the formula. Write: ρ = c(t_r − t_s) + c δt_r, where t_r is the true reception time in system (GPS) time, i.e. the receiver clock reading minus δt_r. Then state in words: measured pseudorange = true range + c δt_r, so a receiver clock that is ahead makes every pseudorange too long and the bias is subtracted when correcting. (Equivalently keep t_r as the clock reading and drop the + c δt_r term.)

problem: 'GNSS computes in WGS84' is too broad. Only GPS is defined in WGS84; GLONASS broadcasts in PZ-90 and Galileo in GTRF, and each receiver converts to a common frame for output.
fix: Say: 'GPS coordinates are expressed in WGS84, a global geocentric datum. Receivers from other constellations transform their positions into WGS84, so GNSS output is normally in WGS84.'
